2. Resolving the Corinthian church's problems
 - Anyway, after sending a letter like this, at first he seemed to feel relieved, but then he kept regretting it. He worried, what if the Corinthian believers read the heated letter and find something else to nitpick? “Say, Titus, come here a moment. You need to go to Corinth for me. Go see how the Corinthian believers are doing, and on your way back, check on the other churches too.”
Unlike Timothy, Titus wasn't one to cry and whine; he was sharp as a razor. Anyway, Paul sent Titus off, and it was time for Titus to come back, but he didn't come. So in the end Paul went up to meet Titus and got as far as Troas, and the people of Troas said, ‘Teacher Paul is here!’ and of course assumed he'd hold meetings and started to get ready, but Paul said, ‘Something urgent has come up, I need to hurry on,’ and passed through. He kept going, Samothrace, Neapolis, Philippi, and around Thessalonica, here comes Titus, la-di-da, strolling up.
“하이고 이 사람아, 아 어떻게 된거야?”: “Oh my goodness, man, so what happened?”
“잘 되긴 뭐가 잘 돼?”: “What do you mean it went well?”
